items.source_label: Vocabulary: Write the Word or Phrase, Question 1–24
items.instruction: Complete each sentence with the word or phrase from the chapter 1–2 vocabulary list. The Swedish cue gives the meaning. Use the list form and write the whole missing word or phrase. Check your spelling. Each gap is worth 1 point.

children.source_label: Vocabulary: Write the Word or Phrase, Question 1

children.source_label: Vocabulary: Write the Word or Phrase, Question 2

children.source_label: Vocabulary: Write the Word or Phrase, Question 3

items.instruction: For each definition, select the correct word or phrase. Each correct match is worth 1 point.

children.prompt:
Select the word or phrase for each definition.
Write the letter of the matching option.
1. absence from school without permission | A. incarceration
2. being kept in a prison or jail | B. truancy
3. a feeling that someone deserves no respect | C. disdain

pairs.left: being kept in a prison or jail
a feeling that someone deserves no respect

children.prompt:
Select the word or phrase for each definition.
Write the letter of the matching option.
1. short of something that is needed | A. evenhanded
2. very fierce, aggressive, or violent | B. ferocious
3. fair to both sides in a disagreement | C. deficient

pairs.left: short of something that is needed
fair to both sides in a disagreement

children.prompt:
Select the word or phrase for each definition.
Write the letter of the matching option.
1. an untrue claim made to deceive someone | A. circumstance
2. another person, whether a friend or a stranger | B. false pretense
3. a condition surrounding a particular event | C. fellow man

pairs.left: an untrue claim made to deceive someone
another person, whether a friend or a stranger
a condition surrounding a particular event

items.instruction: Read each sentence. Choose one option that explains the bold word or phrase as it is used in that sentence.

children.prompt:
Milan tends to boast when he meets new teammates.

What does boast mean here?

Lena made progress through patience and application.

What does application mean here?

The coach’s reversal on weekend training surprised the players.

What does reversal mean here?
choices: a change to the opposite decision
a delay before making a decision
a refusal to discuss a decision
correct_choices: a change to the opposite decision

children.prompt:
Sam seemed to recoil as he lifted the lid.

What does recoil mean here?

Between them, the two cousins saved $80.

Which sentence gives the meaning of between them here?

The report gave a distorted picture of school life.

What does distorted mean here?

items.instruction: Type only the missing word or the replacement requested in each item. Do not copy the whole sentence.

children.prompt:
Write the full form of the bold contraction.
We can’t come to the meeting.
Answer: [___]

Write the full form of the bold contraction.
We’re waiting for your reply.
Answer: [___]

Use a form of book. Write the whole missing word.
I borrowed three [___] from the library.

Use a form of student. Write the whole missing word.
Both [___] finished their work.

Use the present form of walk. Write the whole missing word.
Mia [___] to school every day.

Use the present form of play. Write the whole missing word.
My friends [___] soccer after school every Friday.

The car belongs to one teacher. Complete the sentence with a form of teacher.
This is the [___] car.
notes: The source facit lists “teacher’s” as both the answer and its “Also accepted” variant; the user accepted the straight-apostrophe variant “teacher's” on 2026-10-10.

children.prompt:
The bikes belong to three boys. Complete the sentence with a form of boy.
These are the [___] bikes.
notes: The source facit lists “boys’” as both the answer and its “Also accepted” variant; the user accepted the straight-apostrophe variant “boys'” on 2026-10-10.

children.prompt:
Replace only the bold word. Write one word.
Its time for lunch.
Answer: [___]
notes: The source facit lists “it’s” as both the answer and its “Also accepted” variant; the user accepted the straight-apostrophe variant “it's” on 2026-10-10.

children.prompt:
Write its or it’s.
The school changed [___] lunch menu.

Write most or the most.
[___] students in our class take the bus to school.

Write most or the most.
Of these three questions, this is [___] difficult one.

Use can and you once each to complete the statement. Write only the two missing words.
Tomorrow [___] bring your notebook.

Correct the spelling of the bold text.
We have alot of homework tonight.
Answer: [___]

items.instruction: Choose one answer for each question.

children.prompt: Your e-mail asks the headteacher to put tests on different days. Which subject line states the purpose most clearly?
You are writing a formal e-mail to Ms. Lind. Which greeting follows the class model?
Sam Nilsson is writing a formal e-mail to Ms. Lind. Which complete closing follows the class model?
You ask the headteacher to move some test dates. Which sentence clearly asks for a reply?
choices: Could you discuss the new dates with the other teachers?
Could you add the new dates to the school calendar?
Could you tell me your decision about the new dates?
correct_choices: Could you tell me your decision about the new dates?

children.prompt: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
choices: When I got home, I did my homework.
When i got home, I did my homework.
When I got home, i did my homework.
correct_choices: When I got home, I did my homework.

children.prompt: Which version separates the two complete sentences correctly?
choices: The bus was late, we missed the first lesson.
The bus was late. We missed the first lesson.
The bus was late we missed the first lesson.
correct_choices: The bus was late. We missed the first lesson.
